title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 14/14 — "The Conclusion"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 14, the last. Thursday comes, and there is no need of anyone's evidence: the aneurism has burst in the night, and Jefferson Hope is found on the floor of his cell with a placid smile.

Next evening, by the fire at Baker Street, Holmes shows how simple it was: the narrow wheel marks in the road, two men's boots in the clay of the garden path, a face full of hatred over a body with no wound, a wedding ring that made it a private wrong, a telegram to Cleveland, and a cab-driver who could follow his man through London unseen. Three days, from a result to a name.

Then Watson reads the evening paper, where the credit for the smart capture belongs entirely to Messrs Lestrade and Gregson -- and a certain Mr Sherlock Holmes, an amateur, may in time learn something from such instructors.

Chapter VII of Part Two of Arthur Conan Doyle's A Study in Scarlet (1887), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
